newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine 91-day T-bill rate rises to 10.107 pct.
newsitem.headline: Philippine 91-day T-bill rate rises to 10.107 pct.

text.p: The Philippine benchmark 91-day treasury bill rate soared to an average of 10.107 percent at the regular weekly auction from 9.583 percent last week, the Bureau of Treasury said on Monday.
The other maturities followed suit. The 182-day T-bill rate rose to an average of 10.546 from 10.057 percent; and the 364-day bill jumped to 11.112 from 10.555 percent.
The auction generated 8.405 billion pesos worth of tenders, of which 4.5 billion pesos were accepted.
This is the second straight week that T-bill rates have risen after the Central Bank raised its overnight borrowing rate to 10 from 9.9 percent last Thursday.
"The market is raising its bids because Central Bank raised its overnight rate last Thursday," National Treasurer Caridad Valdehuesa told Reuters after the auction.

The results of the auction were higher than expected. A Reuters poll of five financial institutions last Friday had showed the market had expected the 91-day rate at 9.93 percent; the 182 day at 10.2425; and the 364-day at 10.80 percent.
Government officials said the Central Bank's action was aimed at mopping up liquidity in order to stop speculation amid an expected increase in U.S. interest rates in May.
"Everybody's cautious at this point in time," a foreign bank dealer said.
Traders said some banks had decided to stay away from the auction to see how far rates could rise before investing heavily in the bills.
"Certainly there will be an attraction," Central Bank Treasurer Sergio Edeza told Reuters, referring to the latest T-bill rates.
"It's just for realignment," Edeza said, in reply to a query on why the Central Bank increased its overnight borrowing rate.
